clue.text: Row of futons, perhaps, accommodating men yawning a lot?

indicators.note: the beds take in the men, holding them inside like guests being accommodated

parts.note: futons are an example of beds
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword term for soldiers who are not officers
a row is a quarrel, or tiff

explanation.surface: A line of futons in a dormitory where the men are all yawning their heads off.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order is 'Row of futons', but the beds come first in the answer and the tiff follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thoroughly fed up yawns constantly, so this is a playful illustration of extreme boredom.

clue.text: Cut chapter at start of work

indicators.note: the chapter letters are placed at the beginning of the word for work

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: An editor trims a chapter right at the beginning of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop something is to cut it, typically with a sharp blow; a plain synonym.

clue.text: Cleric working alongside islander

parts.note: a Minorcan is a native of Minorca, the Balearic island
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A clergyman serving side by side with somebody from a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alongside' simply puts the two pieces next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral, below the rank of full canon.

clue.text: Small drink for pet?

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
nog is a strong beer, or eggnog

explanation.surface: A little saucer of something to drink put down for the family pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like a noun for an animal, but it is the verb meaning to kiss and cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet is to kiss and caress amorously, the same informal activity as kissing passionately.

clue.text: One very old classical scholar, outwardly a loner?

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
so means very, as in 'so good'

indicators.note: the scholar sits on the outside, wrapping round the letter for old

parts.note: a Latinist is an expert in the Latin language

explanation.surface: Describing a single elderly scholar of the classics who seems, from outside, to keep to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The O for 'old' lands inside LATINIST, between the I and the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps apart from others in policy or temperament is described by the question-marked example of a solitary type.

clue.text: Starter includes firm, initially tender, steak

indicators.note: the starter dish contains the other pieces, which go inside it

parts.note: an entree is a starter course in British usage
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word tender is used

explanation.surface: A menu where the first course comes with a lovely tender steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' is not a beginning signal here; it means the dish itself, which 'includes' the firm and the first letter of tender.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrecote is a boneless cut of beef taken from between the ribs, a type of steak.

clue.text: Bank invests grand in dynamic Asian economy

indicators.note: to invest is to cloak or surround, so the bank wraps round the letter for grand

parts.note: a tier is a bank, a row set one above another
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Financial news about a bank putting a thousand into a booming Asian market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invests' looks financial but means surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast-growing East Asian economies such as South Korea and Singapore were nicknamed tiger economies.

clue.text: Resistance leader helps in forays

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, taken from Resistance

parts.note: aids means helps, as a verb

explanation.surface: The head of a resistance movement assists in military sorties.
explanation.definitionFit: Raids are sudden attacks or incursions, the same as forays into enemy territory.

clue.text: Old office worker ran out of time unexpectedly

parts.note: ex means former, old, as in ex-husband
a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: the letter for time is left out of the word for ran

parts.note: tore means ran, rushed

explanation.surface: A former secretary who unexpectedly found the clock had beaten her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' drops the T from TORE to leave ORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Done extempore means done on the spur of the moment, without preparation, so unrehearsed and unforeseen.

clue.text: Mistress maybe having no front teeth ate thus?

definitions.meaning: a lover kept secretly besides a regular partner

definitions.text: having no front teeth ate thus?
definitions.meaning: with no incisors you would have to chew with the side teeth, taking bites at the side of the mouth

explanation.surface: Someone without front teeth explains how they managed their meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit on the side is informal slang for a secret lover outside a relationship, such as a mistress.

clue.text: Welshman repulsed scoundrel after removing hat

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the word is read backwards
the hat of a word is its top letter, here dropped from the scoundrel

parts.note: a knave is a dishonest rogue

explanation.surface: A man from Wales drives off a villain once he has taken his cap off.
explanation.walkthrough: KNAVE loses K to give NAVE, which reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Evan is a typical Welsh first name, the Welsh form of John, so a Welshman by example.

clue.text: Team heading off fight, say, in playground

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the team is removed

parts.note: a squad is a team

indicators.note: say signals that the word for fight is to be spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a wrangle is a fight, a noisy argument

explanation.surface: A team stops a scrap breaking out in the school yard.
explanation.walkthrough: WRANGLE spoken loses nothing to the ear without its silent W, giving RANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrangle is a courtyard enclosed by buildings, used in schools as an outdoor play area.

clue.text: Look round part of castle, wanting board and lodging

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for look reads backwards

parts.note: peek means look quickly

explanation.surface: Inspecting a castle tower while hoping for bed and breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting board and lodging' is a second definition: earning your keep means paying for food and lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: The keep is the strongest central tower of a castle, its innermost stronghold.

clue.text: Particular film maker shot one serial, first in Technicolor

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are rearranged
only the opening letter of Technicolor is taken

explanation.surface: A director films a serial, the first one ever made in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like filming but is the anagram signal for ONE SERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Neorealist directors such as De Sica made postwar Italian films of everyday life, a particular school of film makers.

clue.text: Pack up second-rate turkey

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a mob is a pack, a crowd
B is a second-class grade

explanation.surface: Telling someone to quit a mediocre turkey dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack up' looks like a phrasal verb, but up reverses MOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb, like a turkey, is a theatrical or film flop, a total failure.

clue.text: Small animal finally brought under control

indicators.note: in this down clue the last letter goes beneath the word for control

parts.note: to run a business is to control it

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of brought

explanation.surface: A tiny creature at last brought into submission.
explanation.definitionFit: A runt is the smallest, weakest animal in a litter.

clue.text: As writer, achieve comparatively little during insurrection

parts.note: to do is to achieve or accomplish

indicators.note: the smaller amount comes in the middle of the uprising

parts.note: a rising is a revolt or insurrection
less is the comparative of little

explanation.surface: A writer reflects on doing very little in a time of revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' places the comparative inside the uprising word, splitting it after its third letter; 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Lessing was a British novelist and Nobel laureate in literature, so a writer by example.

clue.text: Move slowly, initially turning right on main road, then left

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of turning

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest main road; the 1 stands as letter I

explanation.surface: Directions for a slow drive: turn right onto the main road, then left.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; the figure 1 doubles as I.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail is to lag or drag behind, moving along slowly.

clue.text: Extremely cold potato dish provided during celebration? Not half

indicators.note: the potato dish goes inside the shortened celebration
only half of the word for celebration is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: a festival is a celebration
rosti is a Swiss dish of fried grated potato

explanation.surface: A frozen potato dish served at a party, asking whether it was half-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' drops the second half of FESTIVAL, the IVAL, and 'during' puts the potato dish inside what is left; 'provided' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Frostiest is the superlative of frosty, meaning very cold, so the coldest of all.

clue.text: Master of foxhounds, so to speak, in Cambridgeshire location

parts.note: loosely, belonging to foxhounds means to do with the chase, the sport they serve
a don is a master, a senior academic at a university

explanation.surface: A huntsman leading the hounds through the Fens of eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' admits the whimsy: a master of the hunt is a hunting don, the town's name split in two. Cambridgeshire is an English county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Huntingdon is a market town in Cambridgeshire, England, birthplace of Oliver Cromwell.

clue.text: Assistant to pianist? That's exciting work

definitions.meaning: someone who flips the sheets of music for a performer at the keyboard
a gripping book that you cannot put down

explanation.surface: A pianist's helper turns out to have a thrilling job.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: one turning sheet music for a pianist, and a thrilling book compelling reading.

clue.text: Without hesitation, actors made merry in historical production

indicators.note: without means outside, so the anagram wraps round the hesitation
merry means tipsy, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Performers confidently enjoying themselves in a period drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' looks like 'confidently' but means around UM: ACTORS MADE becomes COST-EDRAMA, split by UM.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume drama is a film or play set in a past era, with period dress.

clue.text: Discover brother stuck in tree, suffering

parts.note: to hear is to discover or learn of something

indicators.note: the brother is lodged inside the tree's name

parts.note: teak is a tropical hardwood tree

explanation.surface: Learning that a sibling is trapped up a tree causes distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak is overwhelming grief or distress, a kind of emotional suffering.

clue.text: Band introduces leading pair of tenors when revealing show

indicators.note: to introduce is to put in, so the band takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a stripe is a band of colour

indicators.note: the first two letters of tenors are taken

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A music group brings on two leading tenors while putting on a revealing performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of musicians beside the tenors, but it means a stripe.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is an act in which a performer gradually undresses, literally revealing.

clue.text: What's regularly offered by couple in parliament? Hospitality

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the words couple in

parts.note: a house is a chamber of parliament, as in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Asking what a parliamentary couple routinely offers its guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's ... offered by' is a link; the alternate letters come from 'couple in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping open house means welcoming all visitors freely, a generous form of hospitality.

clue.text: Extremely severe cardinal maybe turning up for religious ceremony

indicators.note: extremely takes the outermost letters of severe
in a down clue turning up reads the colour upwards, backwards

parts.note: cardinal is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A stern cardinal arrives for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' looks like a churchman but is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seder is the Jewish ritual meal held on the first nights of Passover.

clue.text: Evil guy gobbles up fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read upwards, backwards
the phrase evil guy swallows the run of letters, holding them inside

explanation.surface: A wicked man wolfs down a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo hybrid with wrinkled skin.

clue.text: The others take exam again, but not I

indicators.note: but not means the letter I is excluded from the word for retaking

parts.note: to resit is to sit an examination again

explanation.surface: The rest of the class have to retake a test, though I escape it.
explanation.walkthrough: RESIT is the British term for retaking an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest means the remaining ones, the others in a group.
